rounds.text: Exim Routes Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line scaling, evidenced by 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growths of 146% [E11, E12], alongside a massive 299% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E10]. This fundamental business momentum significantly outperforms the broader sector, where the median profit growth sits at a modest 13.9% and median sales growth is 12.6% [E46, E47]. Furthermore, the company commands a superior capital efficiency advantage with an ROCE of 16.3%, easily besting the sector median ROCE of 6.3% [E6, E48], and maintains a healthy multi-year profitability profile with a 5-year median return on equity of 20% [E14]. Management's forward-looking guidance signals aggressive continued expansion, with a targeted full-year FY27 revenue growth between 30% and 50% aiming to hit Rs. 300 crores at the upper end [E49] and an operational goal to scale container movement to 10,000 units this year [E50]. Conceded: the stock trades at a demanding P/E of 48.5x and exhibits a negative cash conversion of -3.44x due to an operating cash flow of Rs. -15.45 Cr in March 2026 [E1, E20, E21].

Exim Routes Ltd carries a troubling valuation and severe fundamental risks driven by a complete collapse in cash generation, as operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs. 15.45 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs. 26.92 Cr in Mar 2026 [E21, E22]. This translates to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -3.44x against reported profit, with operating cash flow hitting -212% of operating profit [E20, E23], heavily exacerbated by exceptionally high debtor days sitting at 174 days [E37]. Furthermore, institutional investors are fleeing the stock, evidenced by a massive domestic institutional holding drop of 6.05 percentage points and an overall negative institutional money flow signal [E29, E30]. The stock trades at an expensive P/E of 48.5x while offering a 0.00% dividend yield and refusing to pay out dividends despite reported profits [E1, E4, E36]. Valuation models confirm these strains, with a discounted cash flow putting intrinsic value below the market price at Rs. 97 per share, yielding a negative margin of safety of -19.1%, while a reverse DCF indicates the current market price aggressively prices in 20.4% earnings growth [E31, E32, E33]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical top-line and profit growth alongside a conservatively low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16x [E8, E11, E24].

Conceded: the company displays rapid historical sales and profit growth rates such as 299% TTM sales growth [E10] and 146% 3-year profit growth [E12]. However, this hyper-growth has completely broken down the company's operational cash generation, plunging operating cash flow to a severe negative of Rs. -15.45 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -3.44x in March 2026 [E20, E21], which makes the bull's growth narrative a capital-consuming hazard rather than sustainable value creation. While the bull highlights superior ROCE of 16.3% and sector-beating metrics [E6, E48], the company simultaneously suffers from dangerously high debtors averaging 174 days [E37] and a persistent quarter-over-quarter deterioration in operating margins across the last four consecutive quarters [E19]. Furthermore, the market price of Rs. 116 already trades well above its discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs. 97, translating to a negative margin of safety of -19.1% [E31, E32]. Institutional smart money is aggressively fleeing this overvaluation, evidenced by a massive domestic institutional outflow of 6.05 percentage points in a single quarter [E29] that creates a heavily negative institutional money flow signal [E30].

Conceded: the company has posted strong compounded growth rates including 5-year and 3-year profit growths of 146% alongside a 299% jump in TTM sales [E11, E12, E10], and its ROCE of 16.3% exceeds the sector median of 6.3% [E6, E48]. However, this historical momentum masks severe underlying cash collection issues, evidenced by high debtors of 174 days [E37] and a deeply negative operating cash flow of Rs -15.45 Cr in March 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -3.44x [E20, E21]. While the bull highlights ambitious management guidance targeting up to Rs. 300 crores in FY27 revenue [E49] and 10,000 container movements [E50], quarterly operating margins have actually worsened, showing a decreasing trend over the last four quarters [E19]. Furthermore, institutional investors are fleeing this growth narrative, dumping shares to slash domestic institutional holdings by 6.05 percentage points and driving negative money flow [E29, E30]. Finally, investors are asked to pay a steep 48.5x P/E multiple [E1] for a business that offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and trades above its discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 97 [E31], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -19.1% [E32].
